neighbours.label: the point where an inflow is about to be named: the preposition (from, by, with, of, on) after a predicate of being supplied, fed, funded or filled (water from wells, fed by streams, filled with snowmelt, funded by, an influx of); the same prepositions after other predicates stay quiet
fire: The village draws nearly all of its drinking water from a spring in the hills.
The marsh is fed by two slow rivers and a dozen small creeks.
Each April the reservoir is filled with meltwater from the glaciers.
The orchards are irrigated with water pumped from the canal.
The hospital is funded by a mix of state grants and patient fees.
The city obtains most of its electricity from dams on the upper river.
The pond is fed by rain and by runoff from the fields.
The library is funded by a small tax on local property.
quiet: The village sells nearly all of its cheese at a market in the hills.
The marsh was painted by two artists and a dozen students.
Each April the reservoir is closed to boats for the nesting season.
The orchards were planted with care by the first settlers.
The hospital was designed by a team of young architects.
The city hides most of its old charm behind rows of new towers.
The pond was drawn by the children and by their teacher.
The library was praised by a writer in the local paper.

short: inflow / supply source about to be named
notes: Card: prepositions after irrigation, influx, paid for, funded; the - pole's output promotes ' incoming', ' trib', ' freshwater', ' fresh', ' entry'.
